To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factor VITF-1 and three host factors (VITFs-2, 3, and 4) are necessary and sufficient for transcription of intermediate stage promoters by vaccinia virus RNA polymerase.
the HeLa VITF- 2 is G3BP and the p137 protein and that these proteins are sufficient for transcription in vitro of the intermediate stage promoter.
transcription of intermediate stage vaccinia virus genes requires a viral RNA polymerase, three viral transcription factors, a viral capping enzyme, two viral proteins, and two HeLa cell proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cellular factors involved in the regulation of transcription of the DNA genome in the cytoplams.
the identification and characterization of cellular proteins that are essential for the transcription of the vaccinia virus genome.
understanding the mechanisms of transcription of the genome of vaccinia and related orthopoxviruses, and how these mechanisms differ from the transcription of cellular genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VITF-1 and VITF3 are viral proteins, whereas VIT2, which is essential for transcription of linear and nicked circular DNA templates, is a complex of G3BP and P137.

the vaccinia virus intermediate stage transcription is complemented by Ras-GTP-ase-activating proteins SH3 domain binding protein and cytoplasmic activator proliferation associated protein-1, which are involved in the transition between early stage and late stage of the vaccinia virus life cycle.

G3BP and cytoplasmic activator/proliferation associated protein 1 (p137) are essential components of vaccinia virus transcription complex and that they are involved in the transition between early (intermediate) and late phases of the viral cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the viral RNA polymerases are not sufficient to transcribe the intermediate stage genes, and the viral factors are not sufficient to initiate transcription from the intermediate stage promoters.

we have identified the HeLa cell transcription factors VITF-1 and VITF2 as G3BP (Ras-GTPase- activating protein SH3 domain binding protein) and p137 (Cytoplasmic activation/ proliferation associated protein-1) which complement the vaccinia virus RNA polymerase and VITF3 for intermediate stage transcription.
we have identified two novel host proteins that are required for intermediate vaccinia virus transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
two cellular proteins, G3BP and CAP, are essential for transcription of intermediate stage viral genes.
we identified two cellular proteins that are required for intermediate stage transcription of vaccinia virus.
the intermediate stage vaccinia virus transcription is complemented by two host cell proteins, G3BP and P137, which are also required for the formation of stress granules.
